text:
Alex: Ran a short perf sampling run against the batching stress repro (high qps, small seqs). Uploading flame and collapsed stacks. Seeing weird CPU spikes around prefetch + tokenizer.
Mariam: Nice — what was the exact perf invocation?
Alex: ```bash
perf record -F 99 -g --call-graph dwarf -p $(pgrep runtime_worker) -- sleep 60
perf script | ./stackcollapse-perf.pl > out.collapsed
./flamegraph.pl out.collapsed > flame.html
``` 
Alex: Also grabbed a py-spy top/record to cross-check Python frames.
Sam: Quick glance at the collapsed output shows a recurring hotpath: \n```
batch_coordinator::poll -> batch_coordinator::make_batch -> tokenizer::tokenize -> PyEval_EvalFrameEx
kvcache::get -> std::mutex::lock -> futex_wait
```
Sam: Looks like tokenizer takes native time but we also have contention on kvcache locks causing wakeups.
Jin: I replayed perf script with symbols — there are a lot of short samples in `PyThreadState_SetAsyncExc` and C-level GIL acquire. GIL holding seems correlated with prefetch threads that do small token ops in Python.
Lina: Did we enable eager prefetch for small requests? That could multiply Python-side overhead.
Alex: Yes, prefetch threads = 8 by default. On this repro I scaled to 32 to stress it. When I capped to 4 the flame shrank noticeably.
Mariam: Any evidence kernel selector is switching to the heavy attention kernel unnecessarily? That would cost CPU headroom.
Alex: From perf + nvprof traces, kernel_choice logs show we select the 'batched-fused' kernel for seq_len=24 under load due to batching heuristics. But the CPU-side stacking shows most cost occurs before GPU call — in tokenization + scheduling.
Sam: So two issues: 1) Python/tokenization is a larger fraction than we thought; 2) KV cache lock contention / prefetch thread wakeups amplify scheduler churn.
Jin: I pasted a short snippet from collapsed stacks where lock-holder is visible:
```
0x00007f... PyEval_EvalFrameEx (20.5%)
    tokenize_fast
    batch_coordinator::enqueue
    kvcache::get (4.2%)
        std::mutex::lock
``` 
Jin: The lock wait sites align with futex wait times in perf top.
Mariam: Any hypotheses on why tokenizer dominates? Is it Python-level tokenization (our tokenizer wrapper) or external lib?
Alex: It's our thin Python wrapper streaming into the C tokenizer. The wrapper does slicing and pre-checks per chunk — cheap at low QPS but expensive at high concurrency.
Lina: Could we offload tokenization to worker threads (C-level) or batch tokenization before acquiring kvcache? That might reduce GIL pressure.
Sam: Another quick win: reduce prefetch thread count and coalesce kvcache lookups. Our kvcache currently takes separate locks per keyspace, but lookups for small seqs end up serialized on the same lock when keys collide.
Alex: Perf-bot: uploaded flame.html and sample.collapsed to internal perf bucket: https://perf.redwood/internal/1714507890-flame.html :thumbsup:
perf-bot: Note: artifact retention 30d
Mariam: For next runs, can we capture `perf record -e sched:sched_switch` to see wakeup patterns? Also try `perf record -e futex_lock`.
Alex: Will run both. I'll also try swapping tokenizer wrapper with direct C call and re-run to measure drop.
Jin: Proposed action items:\n- Lower prefetch threads default from 8->2 for small-seq profiles (Alex)\n- Coalesce kvcache lookups for batcher (Sam)\n- Add lightweight kernel preference for seq_len < 32 in kernel selector heuristic (Mariam)\n- Prototype C-side tokenization path and measure (Alex)\n- Perf run with sched_switch/futex events and attach (Jin)
Lina: I can add a short A/B test in staging toggling prefetch to verify latency regression risk.
Sam: If we reduce prefetch by default, also add a runtime knob so Dedicated customers can tune it.
Alex: I'll push a short PR to add a `PREFETCH_THREADS` env var and run CI perf harness.
Mariam: Sounds good. Please paste perf artifacts and a 1-line summary in the PR so reviewers know what to look for.
Alex: Will do. Thanks everyone :rocket:
